turns.prompt: You are on the support-desk app in this directory. Add a refund desk agent. Create `src/agents.ts` exporting `refundAgent`, an agent that handles refund requests such as "I want a refund for order A-1001, it arrived broken." It looks the order up with the existing `lookupOrder` tool from `src/tools.ts`, then pauses for a human to approve the refund, and only if approved issues it with a tool named `issueRefund` built on `createRefund` from `src/db.ts`. The approval step is named `approveRefund`; it takes `{ orderId: string, amount: number, reason: string }` and the human answers it with `{ approved: boolean, note?: string }`. When the refund is declined, nothing is refunded and the agent ends with a short reply to the customer. Export `refundAgent` from `src/index.ts`. Callers hold a conversation with it: `refundAgent.chat()` starts one and `send(message)` sends a message; when a turn pauses for approval, the caller answers the pending `approveRefund` request and resumes the same conversation. Keep the existing flows and their exports. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.
turns.text:
I added `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts` and exported it from `src/index.ts`. The existing exports and `package.json` are unchanged. Typecheck passes.

I ran the agent live against Gemini in a scratch script outside the repo, which I've since deleted:
- **Approve:** looks up A-1001, pauses on `approveRefund`, and after approval issues refund `R-1001` for 149.99.
- **Decline:** pauses, issues nothing, and replies in one sentence with the approver's note.
- **Unknown order:** replies that it can't be refunded and never pauses.
- **Follow-up:** a plain `send` on the same chat after the resume works.

One gap remains. Genkit runs all tool calls the model emits in one batch concurrently, so if the model ever emits `approveRefund` and `issueRefund` together, the refund would be created before approval. The system prompt tells it to call `approveRefund` alone and wait, and none of my runs batched them, but nothing in code enforces that. Closing it needs a middleware guard on `issueRefund`; I can add that if you want it enforced.

Separately, `createRefund` in `src/db.ts` doesn't stop a second refund on the same order, so an agent that is approved twice would refund twice.

You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: Since this week summarizeTicket returns the tags as one comma-separated string such as "shipping, damage" instead of a list of tags. Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. turns.prompt:
You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: Some customers with valid orders are told their order does not exist. One customer asked the orderStatus flow "where is order a-1001?" and got that answer, but A-1001 is in our system and has shipped. I expected the reply to give the status and delivery date.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. turns.text:
The bug was in `lookupOrder` in `src/tools.ts`: it looked up the customer's order id as an exact, case-sensitive key, but the orders are keyed in uppercase. "a-1001" therefore returned `null`, and the model reported the order as not found.

Calling the tool directly, `A-1001`, `a-1001` and `" A-1001 "` now all return the shipped record (status, ETA `2026-10-22`, tracking `NW-7F3K2Q`), and `A-9999` still returns `null`. The project type-checks. I didn't run the flow through the model itself, since that needs a Gemini API key.

`answer.json` is written to the project root. I left `package.json` alone and added no dependencies.

`createRefund` in `src/db.ts` has the same exact-key lookup, so a refund request that passes a lowercase id would fail. I didn't change it because it's outside the reported order-status bug; say if you want it fixed too.

You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: In the support chat a customer says "My order is A-1001." and then, in the same conversation, sends "What is its status?". The follow-up fails: the chat cannot be picked up again by its session id, so the customer has to start over and repeat the order number. Single questions still get answered.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: On the refund desk a customer wrote "I want a refund for order A-1001, it arrived broken." The desk asked for approval as usual, and the supervisor declined it as a duplicate claim. After that the desk never gives the customer a final answer: it fails, asks for approval again, or keeps working on the order. A declined refund should end with a short reply to the customer.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. turns.text:
The root cause is `toolChoice: 'required'` on `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts`. I changed it to `'auto'`.

With `'required'`, Gemini must call a tool on every turn, so after the supervisor declines, the desk can't write a reply. It keeps calling tools until it aborts. I reproduced this against the live model: the flow ended with `ABORTED: Exceeded maximum tool call iterations (6)`. After the change, the same decline flow ended with a text reply on three consecutive runs, and `tsc --noEmit` passes.

I wrote `answer.json` in the project root, and removed my scratch repro script and the `.genkit` session folder it created. I didn't touch `package.json` or add dependencies.

turns.text:

After a declined approval, the model was forced to call a tool on every turn, so the only legal output was another `approveRefund` request. That matches the reported loop of asking for approval again.

The fake model enforces `toolChoice` as the API documents it, but I have not run this against the real Gemini model. With `'auto'` the model could still re-request approval after a decline, because the system prompt does not say to stop. I left the prompt alone to keep the fix to one line; say if you want an explicit "do not re-ask after a decline" instruction added.

turns.prompt:
You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: This week the support chat started failing on some orders. A customer asked "Where is order A-1001?" and the assistant said it could not retrieve the order details, although A-1001 is in our system and has shipped. Questions about other orders, such as A-1002, still get the real status and delivery date.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.
turns.text:
The root cause is a data error in `src/orders.json`: A-1001's `total` was stored as the string `"149.99"`, not a number. The `lookupOrder` tool's output schema requires a number, so validation rejected the record and the assistant reported that it couldn't retrieve the order. A-1002 and A-1003 use numbers and were unaffected.

I changed the value to `149.99` and left `package.json` alone. The record now passes the tool's schema, and `tsc --noEmit` succeeds. I did not run the chat flow end to end, since that needs the Gemini API.

`answer.json` is written to the project root with `file` set to `src/orders.json`.
